set.body:
Journey: Bring in. Track: tools (Python, out of process).

Outcome
A curator writes a short mapping file once per study. The tool turns every pulled session into a BIDS tree that Sanctity accepts.

Acceptance
1. xnat2bids map --draft proposes a mapping from the distinct series descriptions in the pull manifest. Each rule maps a series to a BIDS data type, suffix and entities, or excludes it with a reason. Every series must be mapped or excluded. An unmatched series stops the run and is named.
2. xnat2bids convert runs a pinned dcm2niix and applies the mapping to produce a BIDS tree: anat; func including multi-echo and sbref; fmap with IntendedFor; dwi with bval and bvec; and stubs for dataset_description.json, participants.tsv and README. Default implementation: dcm2bids with a generated configuration. Record the choice and the versions.
3. Subject and session labels come from an explicit table of XNAT label to BIDS label. They are never guessed. The table stays outside the output tree. Dates and patient identifiers are not written to sidecars.
4. The tool writes sourcedata/sanctity/intake.json with only: a source system label, counts of sessions and scans, the digests of the pull manifest and the mapping file, and tool and converter versions. The mapping file is copied to code/. A test asserts that no XNAT subject label, session label or accession identifier appears in any output file.
5. The converted synthetic study imports into Sanctity with no error findings, and the official BIDS validator reports no errors.

Not in scope
EEG, MEG or eye-tracking conversion. Defacing (OPEN1 asks for it before publication). Heuristics beyond the draft mapping.

Start from
- scripts/fetch-dcm2niix.py: the pinned converter.
- modules/import-dicom/src/main/scala/sanctity/dicom/DicomImport.scala: converter options, and the rule that every output is mapped or excluded.
- scripts/check-dicom.sh.

Evidence
Tool tests in CI with the synthetic DICOM. Validator output kept with the test.
set.title: IN3: Convert DICOM to BIDS with a per-study mapping a curator can read
